doc.title: Houston Person Part 1 interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Starting on saxophone; mother's piano lessons
summary: Person began seriously at 18 or 19 after hearing jazz through friends and radio; his father bought him a saxophone, and his teacher mother had taught him piano briefly.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: How old were you when you first started playing, and what attracted you to the music? HP I was about 18 or 19, but I’d always been listener of jazz through my friends. Some of my friends introduced me to it, my neighbors, and hearing it on radio, and it just attracted me — the creativeness of it. And my last year in high school, my father got me an instrument for Christmas. Before that I was involved mostly in sports, and we did have a piano in the home. During that time I guess when I was coming along, every home had a piano. And my mother was a school teacher, and she played the piano, so she taught me piano at an early age, which I wasn’t interested in, so I studied for about 5-6 months. And then that was real early. And that after that, much later, I got the saxophone, and that stuck, that stuck. So that’s about 17 or 18, and then I went on to college and really got involved in jazz.
